hypothesis: For a non-increasing protected baseline and time-varying positive asymmetric costs with non-negative budgets, candidate-universal recursive feasibility holds if and only if the clipped lower harm-tube endpoint is non-increasing. Given the previous published output, the exact minimum feasible current budget is c_under_t*max(b_t-p_previous,0).

claimed_results.candidate_universal_feasibility: All candidate sequences remain feasible iff L_t<=L_(t-1) for every t>=2
claimed_results.constructive_failure: If L_t>L_(t-1), choose the preceding candidate at or below L_(t-1), yielding p_(t-1)=L_(t-1) and an empty next interval

information_boundary: The current schedule values may be declared in advance or supplied prefix-causally without accessing outcome y. A full-horizon certificate requires a predeclared schedule; otherwise the implementation checks realized feasibility online and fails closed.

gates: Exhaustive small-grid schedules agree with the candidate-universal lower-bound condition.
Random schedules with non-increasing lower endpoints remain feasible for all tested candidate trajectories and satisfy every online property and pointwise asymmetric harm budget.
Every tested upward lower-endpoint violation admits the frozen constructive candidate counterexample.
The realized-prefix condition exactly matches interval nonemptiness.
The minimum-budget formula is feasible at equality and infeasible immediately below whenever b_t exceeds the previous output.
Changing only the upper cost schedule does not change the feasibility verdict while the directional harm certificate remains valid.
Constant schedules recover the V340 asymmetric and original symmetric APIs exactly.
Non-positive or non-finite costs, negative or non-finite budgets, increasing baselines, and shape mismatches fail closed.
falsification.pass_rule: All gates pass at tolerance 1e-12 and the full existing unit-test suite remains green.
falsification.failure_rule: Any failed gate yields REJECT; do not add the time-varying extension to the manuscript.
